maya: Heads-up — ran into a case where a canary split configured in Console wasn't taking effect because runtime policy had a `force: true` override. Who actually 'owns' the flag when both exist?

sanjay: Depends on source precedence. AFAIK runtime policies are authoritative (safety/operator), console flags are a UI convenience. We never nailed this down in the API though.

liz: Docs are fuzzy. Repro example: console creates feature flag `new_routing: {v1:10, v2:90}` but runtime policy sets `routing_override: {v1:0}` and traffic ends up 100% v2.
```json
// console flag
{"flag":"new_routing","split": {"v1":10,"v2":90}, "source":"console"}
// runtime policy
{"policy":"routing_override","force":true, "split":{"v1":0,"v2":100}, "source":"runtime"}
```

deploy-bot: :rotating_light: deploy 2026-02-15T14:02:12Z — canary rollout started for model-x (id=cr-321).

tom: This is driving noise in dashboards. Console shows intended experiment but telemetry and real traffic show it's suppressed. SREs get alerted on mismatch.

ana: (typo fix) -> ana: We should add an `effective_source` to the rollouts API and return why a console flag is inactive (e.g., "blocked_by_guard", "overridden_by_runtime"). Console can then show a tooltip.

sanjay: +1. Also propose we formalize precedence: guardian/guard rules (safety) > runtime/operator policies > customer reserved (dedicated) > console flags/experiments. That way safety always wins.

kevin: Customers expect console toggles to 'just work' though. Maybe add a `honor_console` boolean on dedicated deployments or a `notify_on_override` flag so toggles fail loudly if blocked.

liz: Another thought — change terminology so we separate: guard (safety), override (operator), experiment (console). Makes policy layer reasoning easier.

maya: Action items from this thread: 1) doc patch to explicitly list precedence and examples, 2) API change to surface `effective_policy_source` + reason, 3) Console UX change to show inactive flags and hover reason, 4) telemetry change to record intended vs realized split. Who can pick up which?

ana: I'll PR the doc patch (small writeup + examples).

kevin: I'll spike the API: return header `x-effective-policy-source` and add `effective_source` + `reason` to /rollouts and /routes responses. Example header: `x-effective-policy-source: runtime`
```http
GET /v1/rollouts/cr-321
x-effective-policy-source: runtime
```

tom: I'll add a telemetry metric `rollout.intended_split` vs `rollout.actual_split` and a dashboard diff panel.

sanjay: Can we also make the runtime produce an audit event when it overrides a console flag (so customers can query it)? If runtime is operator-managed we need that trace.

deploy-bot: :information_source: note added to rollout cr-321 at 2026-02-15T14:02:12Z — "override applied by runtime-policy (force=true)".

maya: Thanks. Let's sync 30m after standup to align APIs and console messaging. I'll draft the doc and link PR here.

kevin: thx. I'll put a short design on the API spike thread and include example responses.

liz: sgtm. small UI copy needed: "This flag is currently inactive due to a safety guard".

maya: Perfect. Closing here, feel free to @channel if you hit blockers. :thumbsup:
